blocking.issue: New regression from the revision. The success cache is now flushed on every snapshot swap and every revocation advance, but the Node hashes only 10 to 20 credentials per second per slot, with max(1, GOMAXPROCS/4) slots and 4 x slots waiters. (1) The revocation flush is not needed: in Figure 2 a cache hit still passes the revocation check (E to F), yet each new `jti`, cut-off or key entry anywhere in the Cluster empties every basic-auth cache on every Node. At one logout revocation per second (hypothesis), the cache never warms, and `auth.basic` throughput falls to the raw hash rate, about 20 to 40 requests per second on an 8-core Node (hypothesis). (2) The swap flush turns every Hot Reload into a burst of RZ-AUTH-007. With 1,000 active basic-auth clients on an 8-core Node (2 slots, 8 waiters), about 990 get 429 at once after the swap, and recovery takes about 25 to 50 s (hypothesis). A Zero-Downtime Upgrade does the same, and it also empties the username LRU, whose new-bucket rate is capped at 100 per second (target). (3) The steady-state capacity is not stated. Entries last 60 s and hits do not extend them, so a Node supports about 60 x hash rate active basic-auth clients: 1,200 to 2,400 on 8 cores (hypothesis), well below the 10,000-entry cache (target). Beyond that, legitimate clients get 429 with no attack at all. (4) 'hashing uses at most a quarter of the cores' is false when GOMAXPROCS is below 4: on a 2-vCPU Node, max(1, 2/4) = 1 slot is half the CPU.
blocking.evidence: Line 402: "| Success cache | HMAC-SHA-256 under a per-process key; 60 s from verification, not extended by hits; 64 shards, 10,000 entries per Node (target); flushed on each snapshot swap and revocation advance; a hit skips throttle and hash |"; line 404: "| Hash queue | max(1, `GOMAXPROCS`/4) slots, which cap the Node's hash rate; 4 × slots waiters, 1 s deadline (target); overflow gets RZ-AUTH-007 unhashed |"; line 409: "At 600,000 iterations a slot verifies 10 to 20 credentials per second (hypothesis), so hashing uses at most a quarter of the cores"; Figure 2: "E -- \"yes\" --> F{\"On the revocation list?\"}".
blocking.fix: (1) Stop flushing on revocation advance, since the revocation check already runs after a cache hit, and say so. (2) On a snapshot swap, keep each entry whose username and stored credential digest are unchanged in the new snapshot, for example by adding the Consumer credential digest to the cache key, and evict only changed or removed credentials. (3) State the steady-state capacity, active basic-auth clients per Node = 60 s x slots x 10 to 20 per second (hypothesis). Also state the post-restart ramp under the 100 per second new-bucket rate (target), and whether a new-bucket overflow returns RZ-AUTH-007 with `Retry-After`. Consider refreshing an entry on a hit up to a hard maximum age, for example 15 minutes (target). (4) Write 'at most a quarter of the cores when GOMAXPROCS is 4 or more, otherwise one core'.

blocking.issue: New regression from the revision. `kid` entries now expire after the maximum token lifetime (24 hours (target)), which contradicts T2. An attacker who holds a leaked IdP private key can mint tokens with any `exp`. A `kid` entry evicts the key only until the next JWKS refresh returns it, and blocks tokens signed with it only while the entry exists. So if the IdP still publishes the key 24 hours after revocation, the leaked key is valid again on every Node, with no alert. The expiry therefore does not end the key's risk, and the T2 mitigation 'kid revocation' stops working after one day.
blocking.evidence: Line 426: "**Expiry.** A `jti` entry MUST carry the token's `exp`, capped at the maximum lifetime, and expires then; cut-offs and `kid` entries expire after that lifetime, and a cut-off meanwhile refuses the subject's tokens without `iat`."; line 92: "| T2 | JWT forgery, leaked IdP key | TB-1, TB-10 | [JWT and OIDC](#jwt-and-oidc); `kid` [revocation](#revocation) |"; line 173: "a `kid` [revocation](#revocation) entry evicts a leaked key."
blocking.fix: Make a `kid` entry permanent until the key leaves the issuer's JWKS. Nodes refuse to load a revoked (issuer, `kid`) from any JWKS fetch and report whether the key is still served. Ruralz Control collects the entry only after no Node has seen the key for one maximum lifetime, and it raises a degraded state and an alert while the IdP still publishes it. Give `kid` entries a small sub-cap within the 100,000 entries, for example 1,000 (target), and let operators remove them manually, with an audited `credential.revoked` collection event.

non_blocking.suggestion: Each entry still carries its own signature. A Node cold-starting or reconnecting against a list near the 100,000-entry cap (target) then verifies up to 100,000 signatures, several seconds of one core (hypothesis). Have the signed high-water mark cover a digest or Merkle root of the entry set, so that a full snapshot needs one verification.

'One shared bucket ... so timing reveals nothing' does not hold under load. An attacker who drains the shared unknown-username bucket then gets an immediate RZ-AUTH-007 for unknown names and a hashed 401 for known ones, which enumerates usernames. Either give unknown usernames per-name buckets derived from a keyed hash, which are indistinguishable from real buckets, or state this residual under OQ-security-and-identity-15.

A default 24-hour maximum lifetime (target) that rejects longer `exp` will break imported deployments whose IdPs issue longer-lived service tokens. Say whether `ruralz bundle import` flags this, and state whether the maximum lifetime is measured as `exp` minus now or `exp` minus `iat`, and whether clock skew applies.

Go has no per-object memory accounting, so 'compiled engine memory ... reported per snapshot' needs a method. Say that `ruralz bundle validate` measures it in isolation, for example as the heap delta around a single-threaded compile, and that Nodes report an estimate. Also say what the 64 MiB ceiling (target) does to the 2 s compile budget (target) in System overview, which excludes cold Plugin compilation but not OPA or Cedar.
'no literal keys in `config`' is now phrased well. Link it explicitly to OQ-wasm-plugin-system-4 option (b), Node-resolved secret fields, so the two documents agree once that question closes.

ac_results.ac: Every KrakenD CE and EE authentication feature (JWT/OIDC/OAuth2, JWT signing, client credentials, revocation bloom filter, mTLS, basic auth, API keys, revoke server, multiple IdPs per KrakenD endpoint, NTLM, GCP auth, AWS SigV4) is mapped to a Ruralz mechanism with a milestone, or marked Not planned with a reason.
ac_results.note: The KrakenD authentication parity table has all 12 rows. NTLM is Not planned, with a reason: it authenticates a connection, and MD4 and HMAC-MD5 violate P1. The other 11 rows carry Planned (M1) or (M2), with pending OQ references where the design is still open.

ac_results.ac: Authorization contains a guidance table comparing CEL, OPA (Rego) and Cedar (when to use, cost, milestone), consistent with ADR-0011.
ac_results.note: The table has When to use, Cost per request (tagged target or hypothesis), Guardrails and Planned columns, and it matches ADR-0011: CEL inline, OPA and Cedar pluggable, no Lua. The engine memory bound now uses (K + 2), in line with System overview and Data plane.

ac_results.ac: The FIPS build statement (GOFIPS140) is consistent with docs/engineering/01-tech-stack-and-libraries.md.
ac_results.note: It matches the tech stack: GOFIPS140=v1.0.0 (CMVP #5247) until v1.26.0 leaves Pending Review, fips140=on and never only, HTTP/3 and hybrid key exchange off, and Plugin cryptography only through a Host Function Capability.

ac_results.ac: Revocation states a propagation-time target tagged (target).
ac_results.note: '5 s or less at p99 with a fresh mark (target)', plus targets for Rollouts, Enrollment identities and operator sessions. The 30 s withholding detection bound (target) is now stated in T17 and Integrity.

ac_results.ac: Compliance contains an audit event catalog with at least 15 events.
ac_results.note: 18 table rows covering 24 named events, and the min_table_rows check passes.

ac_results.ac: Transport security covers TLS 1.3, mTLS, certificate rotation and HTTP/3.
ac_results.note: The hop table and the Mutual TLS, Certificate rotation, HTTP/3 and FIPS build subsections are all present, and the Hot Reload mode change now sets Connection: close on busy HTTP/1.1 connections.

ac_results.note: The section covers RBAC rules, OIDC and SAML SSO Planned (M5), the audit log with off-box chain heads, the ADR-0017 trust policy table, and Release supply chain with a CycloneDX SBOM and SLSA Build Level 3.

foundation_amendments: Configuration model `auth.jwt` issuers[] (via OQ-security-and-identity-1): add a per-issuer maximum token lifetime and an 'exp required' rule. The revocation expiry rules and RZ-AUTH-003 depend on them.
